title: Darkshore
body: Darkshore is a long strip of coast on the northwestern edge of Kalimdor, a cold and misty country of grey beaches, rocky bluffs and dark evergreen woods pressed against the mountains to the east. Ten thousand years ago it was a rich land of the kaldorei empire, and Queen Azshara's Highborne dwelt in the twin towns of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran, and the city of Mathystra shone in the north. The Sundering left them in ruins, and their restless dead still walk among the stones. Today the night elves hold only the port of Auberdine, and the land around it is sickening. Fel moss spreads through the woods, a taint from Felwood fouls the Cliffspring River, a plague has turned the thistle bears rabid, the deer are sickly, the moonkin grow hostile and the Blackwood furbolgs are openly hostile. Stormscale naga haunt the northern ruins, Greymist murlocs raid the shore, the Twilight's Hammer camps at the Master's Glaive and a warlock cult has gathered at the Tower of Althalaxx. In the remote far northeast, the Shatterspear trolls keep to themselves.

title: Auberdine
body: Auberdine is the only night elf town on the Darkshore coast, a port of low, arched timber halls among the pines, lit by lamps and guarded by Sentinels. Elder Thundris Windweaver sees to its affairs beside a village council, while Sentinels Glynda Nal'Shea and Elissa Starbreeze see to its defense. Trade has drawn others: dwarves of the Stonehammer and Steelhand families teach mining and smithing and sell their wares, and a gnome tinkers near the inn. Three docks serve the town. From the northern pier the Moonspray sails for Rut'theran Village, from the southern the Bravery crosses to Stormwind Harbor, and from the western pier Elune's Blessing carries travelers to Azuremyst Isle. A moonwell and a lighthouse stand nearby.

title: Mist's Edge
body: North of Auberdine, Mist's Edge is the longest stretch of Darkshore's coast, a run of gloomy bays and grey beaches where crabs scuttle over the sand and Greymist murlocs keep their camps. The waters are worse. Threshers and coastal frenzies hunt offshore, and two ships, the Silver Dawning and the Mist Veil, lie on the seabed north of the town, sunk with their captains when murlocs fell on them as they sailed in. Their logs still rest below in lockboxes. Farther north, a shipwrecked self-styled pirate, Captain Gelkak Gyromast, curses the threshadons that sank his ship and wants his mechanical first mate, the Threshwackonator 4100, put back in working order.

title: Cliffspring River
body: The Cliffspring River runs down from the eastern mountains to empty into the sea at Mist's Edge, north of Auberdine. Its waters were once pure, but they have begun to turn foul, and Thundris Windweaver fears the wash will soon reach the town. A sample drawn from the pool beneath the first waterfall upriver, where a bridge crosses overhead, proved putrid, and Thundris traces the taint east to Felwood. Along the banks stands the northern camp of the Blackwood furbolgs, its stores of fruit, nuts and grain heaped near a bonfire by the water, with warriors and totemics of the tribe keeping watch.

title: Cliffspring Falls
body: Cliffspring Falls spills from the mountains east and a little north of Auberdine, the source of the Cliffspring River. Behind the falling water lies a cave where rare mushrooms grow, scaber stalks and death caps that Barithras Moonshade needs for a potion. The Ancients of the Grove warned him to stay away, sensing that the cave hid a new evil in Darkshore, and their fears were well founded. Stormscale naga, wave riders and sirens, have made the cavern their lair, among them one known as Lord Sinslayer, and thugs of the Twilight's Hammer have been seen in their company.

title: Bashal'Aran
body: Bashal'Aran was one of the twin towns Queen Azshara gave to her Highborne, ruled with Ameth'Aran by Athrikus Narassin and home to his second, the mage Asterion. Both towns fell when the Well of Eternity was destroyed. Its broken stones east of Auberdine are now overrun by vile sprites, wild grells and Deth'ryll satyrs, minions of the demons who feed on the magic lingering in the ruins and grow stronger for it. There is one shrine they will not approach. On a small bluff on the western side, a strange blue aura hangs between the pillars, and within it the spectral Asterion has been held prisoner for more than a thousand years.

title: Tower of Althalaxx
body: The Tower of Althalaxx rises in the north of Darkshore, northeast of Auberdine, some way removed from the twin towns it once watched over. Athrikus Narassin, Azshara's governor of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran, spent most of his days here rather than among the people he ruled. Ten thousand years later the tower is occupied again. Warlocks calling themselves the Cult of the Dark Strand have gathered around and inside it, fanatics and voidcallers with a satyr, Delmanis the Hated, among them, while the most powerful keep to the upper rooms. From hiding in the nearby woods, Balthule Shadowstrike watches the cult and sends word of it to Auberdine and to his master in Ashenvale.

title: Ruins of Mathystra
body: At the northern end of Darkshore lie the Ruins of Mathystra, once a great bastion of the night elves. The city was shattered when the Well of Eternity was destroyed, and its survivors left for smaller villages along the coast to the south. Its glory has faded, but shards of its magic remain in the relics and small cat figurines scattered among the grass and broken stones. The Stormscale naga hold the ruins now, myrmidons, sorceresses and warriors guarding them fiercely, and a naga called Lady Vespira among them. Onu of the Grove of the Ancients wants the relics studied, fearing that the Twilight's Hammer means to turn this old elven magic to its own ends.

title: The Long Wash
body: The Long Wash is the shortest stretch of Darkshore's coast, running south from Auberdine, a gloomy shore strewn with debris and the carcasses of sea creatures. Great beasts of the sea have been beaching themselves here in growing numbers, and the skeleton of a sea turtle lies in the water west of the town beside a sunken ship. Greymist murlocs and crawlers pick over the sand. In the shallows lie crates of elunite ore, spilled long ago when a ship broke on the rocks near the Auberdine lighthouse, still guarded by the cursed Shade of Elura.

title: Ameth'Aran
body: Ameth'Aran lies east of the road south of Auberdine, twin to Bashal'Aran and once a town where Azshara's Highborne practiced their powerful magic freely. When the Well of Eternity was destroyed it fell to ruin, and its people did not rest. Cursed, writhing and wailing Highborne spirits still drift among the broken walls, wielding the magical implements they used in life, and one called Lady Moongazer walks among them. Two great tablets here tell of the town and its fall. In the ruins still burns an ancient blue flame, a fire in which Asterion's moonstone seal can be destroyed, and somewhere among the restless dead wanders the spirit of Anaya Dawnrunner.

title: Twilight Vale
body: Twilight Vale is the southern forest of Darkshore, stretching from below Ameth'Aran toward the Ashenvale border, its woods cut by the Wildbend River. Travelers do best to keep to the road. Rabid and grizzled thistle bears, moonstalkers and foreststriders roam beneath the trees, many of the deer are sick, and the Blackwood furbolgs, once friends of the night elves, prowl the vale in numbers, among them a brute called Carnivous the Breaker. Sentinel Tysha Moonblade keeps a lonely post by the road. Farther south, near the border, a Sentinel carrying word to Auberdine was ambushed and poisoned by furbolg trackers.

title: Grove of the Ancients
body: Nestled against the mountains due south of Auberdine, the Grove of the Ancients is a sacred place built among the ruins of an old night elf temple. Here dwells Onu, an Ancient of Lore, patient and wise. The night elves of Auberdine count the Ancients as venerable allies and heed their warnings. Onu had long awaited a message from the Arch Druid in Darnassus, and he keeps a wary eye on the Twilight's Hammer at the Master's Glaive to the south. Two merchants keep a small camp in the grove, and Kerlonian Evershade, a Druid of the Claw still drowsy from the Emerald Dream, has stopped here for a nap.

title: Blackwood Den
body: Blackwood Den is a cave of the Blackwood furbolgs in southern Darkshore, south of Auberdine and a short way off the road. Ursa and shamans of the tribe hold it, and they have no welcome for strangers. Volcor, master of the bear Grimclaw, was wounded by the furbolgs and trapped inside, unable to win his way out alone. Grimclaw went north to Auberdine for help, and afterwards waited by the roadside to show a rescuer the way to his master. Getting out again meant fighting a path down to the road, or slipping past the furbolgs unseen.

title: The Master's Glaive
body: In the south of Darkshore a vast blade stands driven into the earth. This is the Master's Glaive, marking the place where one of the old lords of the earth, defeated long ago, was impaled and fell. The lord is long dead, but Onu fears that slivers of its power remain, and the Twilight's Hammer, who worship such ancient masters, have come for them. Thugs and disciples of the cult camp at the site now, crying glory and blood for the Old Gods, a firecaller named Radison among them, and in their camp lies a maddening tome written in an ancient elven tongue. A wanderer named Therylune strayed too close and found herself surrounded.

title: Remtravel's Excavation
body: In southwestern Darkshore, near the coast, the Explorers' League opened a dig under Prospector Remtravel, famed at the academy in Ironforge for his discoveries. The dwarves uncovered evidence of a great society, and then horrible golems sprang from the ground and overran the site. Cracked golems and stone behemoths still lumber among the tents. His assistant Hollee fled to Auberdine for help. Remtravel, oblivious as ever, stayed behind, chiseling at the stone and hunting for his stone brush and for a mysterious fossil he had promised to send the League.

title: Twilight Shore
body: The Twilight Shore is the long southern coast of Darkshore, running from west of Ameth'Aran down to the Ashenvale border. Greymist murlocs have built hutted camps along the sand. One of them is the haunt of Murkdeep, for whose death the Auberdine Village Council has offered a reward, and another murloc, Flagglemurk the Cruel, prowls the beaches farther north. Near the border, naga of Blackfathom and Fallenroot satyrs lurk at the water's edge, kin to those in the drowned ruins on the Ashenvale coast. The fisherman Heldan Galesong casts his line here all the same.

title: Thundris Windweaver
body: Thundris Windweaver serves as elder of Auberdine, offering sage and just stewardship of the village's daily affairs. He sees the dangers plainly: dark forces at the borders, ancient taints resurfacing and new evils rising to topple the balance of the land. He wants the Highborne implements of Ameth'Aran destroyed so the horrors of the past are not repeated, and he traced the fouling of the Cliffspring River to Felwood. His friendships reach far. Through his old friend Huntress Kella Nightbow came a letter from the draenei of Blood Watch proposing an alliance, and he recognized among the draenei's foes some ancient enemies of his people. Raene Wolfrunner insists she once saved his life.

title: Onu
body: Onu is an Ancient of Lore who dwells in the Grove of the Ancients, patient, wise and sparing with his words. The wind whispers to those who listen, he says, and he listens. He had long awaited word from Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm, and when the message finally came he remarked mildly that the Arch Druid always seems in such a hurry, when the forest knows that all shall come to pass in its appointed time, as Shan'do Stormrage understood. Onu finds it strange that naga have come to Darkshore, and stranger still the Twilight's Hammer. He speaks to those who help him through scrying bowls and weighs what they bring in long meditation.

title: Terenthis
body: Terenthis, a druid, has come to Auberdine to learn how far the fel moss has spread through Darkshore, for the corruption of Teldrassil and the lands around it troubles the druids of the Cenarion Circle and all night elves. Some of his brethren were rescued from a corrupt furbolg on Teldrassil, and he has vowed to stop such atrocities before more of his kind are hurt or worse. He began with the Blackwood furbolgs, and what he found confirmed his fears. He takes no pleasure in killing the creatures of the forest, but with no cure yet found he believes the corruption must be held back. When the bear Grimclaw came roaring into town, a spell let Terenthis understand him.

title: Asterion
body: Asterion was second to Athrikus Narassin when the Highborne governed the twin towns of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran, a mage known for his physical prowess as much as his arcane art, who lived among the people of Bashal'Aran and saw to their needs. Athrikus imprisoned him with a moonstone seal, and when his long life ended he found himself still captive, a specter caged by the pillars of a shrine. For a thousand years and more he has stared at them. His courtesy has grown dry and barbed, and he fears his mind may never recover. Freed at last, he recalls a world where the Well still stood and Azshara held court, and he senses that his old master yet lives.

title: Athrikus Narassin
body: Athrikus Narassin was a favorite of Queen Azshara, set over the twin towns of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran, though he preferred the solitude of his Tower of Althalaxx to the people he ruled. When the Sundering came and Ameth'Aran lay in ruins, he appeared among its terrified people with a promise: by his spell they would have life eternal, while all around them perished. Highborne souls have been trapped in his soul gems ever since, feeding his power. He bound his own second, Asterion, with a moonstone seal. Ten thousand years on, this ancient and powerful warlock leads the Cult of the Dark Strand from the top of his tower, ringed by his strongest followers.

title: Cerellean Whiteclaw
body: Cerellean Whiteclaw loved Anaya Dawnrunner of Ameth'Aran in the age when the Well of Eternity still stood. After the battles at the Well of Eternity he heard that her town had been destroyed and its people killed, Anaya among them, and in his grief he followed Shan'do Stormrage into the long sleep, taking his sorrow into his dreams through the passing of the ages. Thousands of years later her memory still haunted him. Wandering the woods of Darkshore in a daze, he came upon the ruins and saw her spirit there, haunted and restless. He knew she must be freed but could not raise his hand against her. When she was released at last, her final words were for him.

title: Prospector Remtravel
body: Prospector Remtravel of the Explorers' League is a legend at the academy in Ironforge for his great discoveries, and a trial to anyone who works beside him. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker assigned Hollee to work under him in Darkshore, and their dig soon turned up evidence of a great society. When golems burst from the earth and overran the site, Hollee ran for help, while Remtravel never seemed to notice. He mistakes strangers for Hollee, loses his stone brush and the fossil he promised the League, stops to admire his copy of Green Hills of Stranglethorn, and pauses mid fight to inspect a mossy stone. Hollee despairs of him.

title: Volcor and Grimclaw
body: Volcor travels the Darkshore woods with his bear Grimclaw, and can take a beast's shape himself when he needs to run. The Blackwood furbolgs wounded him in the south and cornered him in a cave, too hurt to break out alone. Grimclaw went for help, bursting into Auberdine and roaring and stamping at Terenthis until he was understood. Terenthis sewed a cloak of moonstalker pelts enchanted so that the wearer could pass Darkshore's creatures unhindered, and a rescuer wrapped in it found the bear waiting by the road. Grimclaw led the way, and at the sight of his master he rushed forward and licked his face. The two then escaped together, by force or by stealth.

title: Wizbang Cranktoggle
body: Wizbang Cranktoggle is a gnome inventor living in Auberdine, proud of his newest creation, the buzzbox, a box with levers that lets people talk across great distances. He has set several around Darkshore, each placed near the creatures whose parts will fix its particular fault, and each, he claims, in constant need of repair. As each box hums back to life his voice through it grows more slurred, broken by hiccups and loud gulping. The truth comes out at last. The buzzboxes also brew and distill fine liquor, a trade the night elves do not appreciate in their towns, and Wizbang happily sings the praises of crawler wine, thresher ale and moonstalker moonshine.

title: Murkdeep
body: Murkdeep is a murloc with a price on his head. The Auberdine Village Council holds him responsible for the death of at least one Sentinel and suspects him of sinking at least two cargo vessels in the waters off Darkshore. He was last seen at a hutted murloc camp on the shore south of the town, thought to be guarding its huts. He keeps out of sight there until the camp's warriors and hunters have fallen, then comes out to fight. The bounty is to be claimed from Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea, who promises that the townsfolk will sleep a little more soundly and safely once he is dead.

title: The Twilight's Hammer at the Master's Glaive
body: It began with mushrooms. Barithras Moonshade of Auberdine needed rare fungi from the cave behind Cliffspring Falls, but the Ancients had warned him away, sensing that a new evil hid there. Whoever gathered them saw what lurked inside, and soon Onu himself asked to speak with them. Onu thought it strange that naga had come to Darkshore, but stranger still the Twilight's Hammer, a cult that worships old lords of the earth defeated long ago. One such lord fell at the Master's Glaive, and Onu sent his visitor there with a phial of scrying, to speak with him through a bowl. The cultists were indeed at the Glaive, seeking the slivers of power the dead lord left behind. In their camp lay a tome of maddening script, and the one page that could be torn from it proved to come from an ancient elven text: the cult was using elven magic to bring its masters back. Onu then sent for relics from the Ruins of Mathystra, hoping to unlock that magic before his enemies could.

title: The Absent Minded Prospector
body: Archaeologist Hollee had been proud to be assigned to the famous Prospector Remtravel, and the dig in southern Darkshore had gone well, turning up evidence of a great society. Then horrible golems sprang from the ground and overran the site. Hollee ran to Auberdine for help, while Remtravel stayed behind, apparently never noticing the danger. When her plea was answered, the prospector was found still at his stones, mistaking his visitor for Hollee and fretting over a lost stone brush and a mysterious fossil he had promised the Explorers' League. Searching for it meant guarding him through the ruined camp while golems and beasts came at him from every side, and as he wandered from tent to stone he finally remembered that he had given the fossil to Hollee all along. Hollee would not leave Darkshore without him, so the fossil was carried to the League in Darnassus, and from there its trail led on across the sea to Menethil Harbor.

title: The Blackwood Corrupted
body: Terenthis began his inquiry into Darkshore's corruption with the furbolgs, and the Blackwood camp south of Auberdine showed it plainly. With the tribe so close to the town he asked for its pathfinders and windtalkers to be thinned, grieving the need, since no cure had been found for the fel moss loose in the forest. His findings went to Thundris Windweaver, who suspected the Blackwood were not the true root of the evil. The Cliffspring River, fouling near the tribe's northern camp, pointed east to Felwood, and in time it emerged that satyrs held the furbolgs in thrall through talismans that channel their magic. A bowl of moonwell water mixed with the tribe's own fruit, nuts and grain, set by the bonfire at the river camp, cleansed the furbolgs who ate just long enough to draw out the satyr corruptor, Xabraxxis. His Talisman of Corruption came back to Auberdine: one battle won in the war to reclaim the forest, and some hope that the Blackwood may yet be freed.

title: The Fall of Ameth'Aran
body: Sentinel Tysha Moonblade was sent to explore Ameth'Aran and found two great tablets, but the Highborne spirits fell on her as she read them and she fled. Their words, once deciphered, give the Circle of Ancients a rare record of the War of the Ancients. The Lay of Ameth'Aran tells how the children of the stars built their homes on the shores of the Well, where Elune was said to rest, and how Azshara set Athrikus Narassin over the twin towns, with Asterion as his second. The Fall tells of ancient trees uprooted, a sky torn by magic and brother fighting brother. As Ameth'Aran lay in ruins, Athrikus appeared and promised its people, with a spell, life eternal. In Auberdine, Thundris Windweaver wants the magical implements their restless spirits still wield taken and destroyed, so that their long dormant evil is never released again.

title: The Prisoner of Bashal'Aran
body: Thundris Windweaver had noticed that the demons infesting Bashal'Aran shunned one shrine, a small bluff on its western side bathed in a strange blue aura. Within waited Asterion, a Highborne specter whose dry courtesy could not hide centuries of torment. A seal held him there, and he asked for help finding it. The earrings worn by the grells carried a trace of it, enough to show that the seal had passed to the satyrs who led them, and from a Deth'ryll satyr came the Ancient Moonstone Seal itself, the work of one of the mightiest of the Highborne. It could be unmade only in the ancient blue flame that still burns in Ameth'Aran, twin of his town. When the seal was destroyed, Asterion was free for the first time since the Well of Eternity stood. He named his jailor, his former master Athrikus, sensed that he still lived, and felt his despair give way to thoughts of vengeance.

title: The Tower of Althalaxx
body: Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze, charged with keeping Auberdine from harm, had sent Balthule Shadowstrike to watch the strange happenings at the Tower of Althalaxx, and when he was long overdue she sent someone to find him. He had stayed at his post, afraid to miss something. Warlocks had gathered around and inside the tower, and parchments taken from them gave the company a name, the Cult of the Dark Strand, though Balthule knew nothing of its history. His master Delgren the Purifier, a paladin who helps the Sentinels against demons and undead, had suspected such a gathering, and Balthule's letter went south to him in Ashenvale, where the hunt for the cult's power carried on. When it was done, Balthule had news of his own: a blinding flash from the upper room of the tower, then screams and lightning striking the ground. The time had come. Athrikus Narassin fell at the top of his tower, and word went south to Delgren that the Cult of the Dark Strand was beaten and scattered.

title: Tharnariun's Hope
body: A sickness has spread across Darkshore, gripping the minds and bodies of all it touches, and the thistle bears have suffered worst, once noble beasts made rabid and frenzied. Tharnariun Treetender of Auberdine hoped he had a cure. A trap of light laid in the forest calmed a rabid bear long enough to be led back to him, but the cure failed. With sorrow he ordered the sick bears put down, knowing it would only slow the plague's damage for a time, and at last sent his helper to a cave near Bashal'Aran to slay the infected Den Mother, from whom ever more rabid bears were spreading into the land. He gave thanks for those who answered his call, for in these war torn lands, he said, many choose to hide in their homes or flee to the safer lands of the Alliance.

title: Washed Ashore
body: Great creatures of the sea have long been known to fling themselves onto the Darkshore coast and die there, but lately they have been washing ashore in ever greater numbers. The Temple of the Moon sent Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde to Auberdine to learn why. Greymist murlocs made her work hard, ringing a giant carcass on the beach south of the town, so she asked for help gathering its bones to send by hippogryph to Darnassus. A second find, the remains of a sea turtle in the water west of Auberdine near a sunken vessel, gave her a real chance at the mystery, and she asks to hear of any other beached creatures along the coast. The idea that troubles her most is that the creatures may be fleeing the waters around Teldrassil. She cannot help thinking the strandings are an ill omen.

title: The Red Crystal
body: The moonkin of Darkshore were once thought gentle, almost mystical creatures, and some still revere them, but Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea must keep Auberdine safe, and hostile moonkin now roam east of the town in growing numbers. Reports claimed they were being drawn to a large red crystal along the eastern mountains, though no one knew whether it even existed. It does. Glynda, who suspects it is tied to Felwood above, had moonwell water poured over it, and its opaque surface turned clear to reveal small fragments of bone and half a jawbone, seemingly a humanoid's, locked inside a stone that even strong magic could hardly break. The answers raised only more questions. Glynda took them to the town council, content for now that the threat lay far enough to the east.
